frameworks.framework: College, Career, and Civic Life (C3) Framework for Social Studies State Standards
frameworks.note: Unlike math and ELA, the United States has no single national social studies standard. The C3 Framework is the closest equivalent and is the reference most state standards are built against, so it is used here. C3 publishes indicators in K-2, 3-5, 6-8, and 9-12 grade bands; each band is split across its grades so no grade repeats another's standard set. The 9-12 band divides naturally by disciplinary strand: Geography to World Geography, History to World and US History, and Civics plus Economics to Government and Economics.
frameworks.subject: Social Studies
frameworks.textFidelity: Indicator codes are verbatim. Text is faithful to the published indicators; longer indicators are abridged for display in a mastery map. Verify against the source URL before any public-facing use.

frameworks.framework: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts
frameworks.note: CCSS publishes high school ELA in 9-10 and 11-12 grade bands rather than by grade. Because mastery is permanent in Supernova, assigning an entire band to both of its grades would leave every 10th and 12th grader with a pre-mastered standard set. Each band is therefore split by strand cluster: grades 9 and 11 carry the Key Ideas and Details standards, grades 10 and 12 carry Craft and Structure plus Integration of Knowledge. Standards naming American literature and US foundational documents are assigned to grade 11 (American Literature), where they belong.

frameworks.framework: National Core Arts Standards - Visual Arts
frameworks.note: NCAS publishes performance standards grade by grade for PreK-8, then at three proficiency levels for high school rather than by grade, recognizing that high school arts coursework is not organized by grade. Those levels map to the course sequence as follows: Art I and Art II to HS Proficient (HSI), Art III to HS Accomplished (HSII), and Art IV to HS Advanced (HSIII). Because Art I and Art II share the Proficient level, the level's standards are split between them by artistic process so neither course repeats the other. The four artistic processes are Creating (Cr), Presenting (Pr), Responding (Re), and Connecting (Cn).

frameworks.note: NGSS publishes middle school (MS-) and high school (HS-) performance expectations in grade bands rather than by grade. Middle school follows the common Earth (6) / Life (7) / Physical (8) rotation so each grade carries a distinct set. High school maps by domain onto the Biology-Chemistry-Physics sequence, with Environmental Science drawing on Earth and Space Science plus ecosystem standards.

frameworks.framework: SHAPE America National Standards and Grade-Level Outcomes for K-12 Physical Education
frameworks.note: SHAPE America organizes high school outcomes into Level 1 (the graduation expectation) and Level 2 (beyond graduation expectation) rather than by grade. Physical Education 9 and 10 use Level 1 outcomes; Fitness and Wellness (11) and Lifetime Fitness (12) use Level 2. Standards are split across the paired grades so no grade repeats another's set. SHAPE released revised national standards in 2024; this prototype uses the 2014 edition because its grade-level outcome structure is the one most districts currently report against.
